teamCompiledPaper.title: Optimal Sensor Placement for Wastewater Network Monitoring
teamCompiledPaper.description: Compiled team review of where to place a small number of sensors in a wastewater network. It covers sensor technologies, placement and optimisation methods, sewer condition and failure factors, and the openly available South Australian network data. The review finds that the best location depends on what the sensor must detect (level trend, overflow alarm, flow, contaminant or gas), and that published percentage gains are network-specific. It sets out a staged, purpose-specific placement method to be tested on the SA Water network.

teamProjectReport.title: Project Report and Handover: Optimal Sensor Placement for Wastewater Network Monitoring
teamProjectReport.description: Team report on the engineering work: a browser-based sensor-placement sandbox built on openly published South Australian sewer data for the Walkerville council area, three EPA SWMM hydraulic simulation studies, and the public site that presents them. It covers the data, models, algorithms, results, verification, assumptions and limitations, and how to reproduce, run and extend the work. It is the companion to the team compiled paper.
